stemMarkdown: A 75-litre solution contains 36% acid. How many litres of water must be added to dilute it to a 15% acid solution? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The acid stays fixed at $27.00$ litres. For that to be $15\%$ of the solution, the total volume must become $\dfrac{27.00 \times 100}{15} = 180.00$ litres. Water to add $= 180.00 - 75 = 105.0$ litres.
altSolutionMarkdown: Only the solvent changes — anchoring on the unchanged solute is what makes these quick.
